reason: The only change item on this feature is the 2025-11-26 launch the claim describes; the later items (DNS Firewall, Outposts, Global Resolver, TLDs, IPv6) do not touch it, and a changes search for accelerated recovery finds only the launch. The developer guide still states the 60-minute RTO, the Oregon copy and the turn-on-before-an-issue condition.

The 2026-05-11 announcement is the newest statement on the Advanced and Foundational tiers; the later items (PANW GA 2026-09-29, analytics 2026-10-01) add integrations and do not rename or replace the tiers.

The claim already states the July 2023 history entry as dated history and then gives the present state (Local Zone Group in geoproximity records, Local Zones enabled first), which the current geoproximity pages quote. The newer 2023-10-19 What's New item extends traffic flow geoproximity to Local Zones and does not contradict it.
The 2026-05-07 announcement is the only statement about DNS64 on inbound endpoints and IPv6 forwarding through the IGW on outbound endpoints; no later change item replaces it.

The 2025-11-30 announcement and the current guide page (What is Route 53 VPC Resolver) both state the rename. Global Resolver GA on 2026-03-09 does not reverse it; some later What's New titles still say 'Route 53 Resolver' as a loose name, which does not replace the claim.

The claim is scoped to what the FAQ answers, and the current saved FAQ still reads 'As of today, bias can only be applied to geoproximity rules.' A corpus search finds no newer or conflicting statement, and no change item adds bias to another rule type.

The claim marks the whitepaper as historical reference only and dates the Resolver query logs support to the 2020-09-01 history entry; the current Resolver query logging page still lists the three query sources named. No change item replaces this.
